sentences.text: Since July 1987, the provincial government showed its commitment to HIV/AIDS through the development and continued operation of the Provincial AIDS Program through Alberta Health.
Shortly after the introduction of the Program, a strategic plan for the prevention, management and control of AIDS was released by the government.

The Provincial AIDS Program, in collaboration with other government departments, professional experts, community organizations and affected individuals and families, made a great deal of progress in addressing HIV/AIDS issues.

Alberta's Health Goals developed in 1993 identified reducing the rate of HIV infections as an objective, with actions to achieve this objective identified under goals for choosing healthy behaviours such as healthy sexual relationships that include avoidance of risky sexual behaviours and developing skills for facing challenges of life in healthy ways.

The Provincial AIDS Program addressed the prevention, management and control of HIV/AIDS through well planned education, care and support strategies, facilitated by substantial financial commitments by the government.

Major prevention components of the Provincial AIDS Program included provision of resources to schools such as print, video, and special programs like the 'I Care' project in cooperation with Alberta Education.

The Provincial AIDS Program provided community organization grant funding of $665,000 primarily to the 10 AIDS organizations, the injection drug use programs in Edmonton and Calgary, and small grants to rural committees.
The Provincial AIDS Program supported regional health authorities' HIV prevention activities through print and audiovisual resources, workshops and presentations, and funding of $235,000.
The Provincial AIDS Program operated a toll-free AIDS/STD information line that received about 2,500 calls monthly.
The Provincial AIDS Program ran the FACING AIDS multimedia campaign which in 1995 was carried by 13 TV stations, and 40 weekly and 7 daily newspapers for a 26-week series.
The Provincial AIDS Program implemented a young adults' program as a 3-year initiative for 18-26 year olds through community and corporate partners.
The Provincial AIDS Program provided HIV antibody testing through Provincial Labs and counselling by doctors requesting the tests.
